name: Samaria Modern
overview: Samaria was repopulated by various nations brought by the king of Assyria, who settled in its cities after the exile of Israel, as recorded in 2 Kings 17. These peoples feared the LORD but also served their idols, continuing the idolatrous practices of their ancestors. After the exile, Samaritans sought to join in the worship of the God of Israel, claiming a shared devotion since the days of Esarhaddon king of Assur, yet their religion remained mixed with idolatry. The hostility between Samaritans and Jews is evident in the opposition faced by the Jews during the rebuilding of Jerusalem’s wall, exemplified by Sanballat’s anger and mockery in Nehemiah 4.
